purpose: Test whether low acoustic phase differences add cross-portion predictive information about multiband idle power, before constructing another sound.
source: Reuse frozen native F2 6..9s training and previously inspected 9..12s check, and all three original common-LR same-PSD phase controls. No new source, interval, phase extraction or frequency fit.
architecture: Nested native model: DC plus real/imag of three existing low-mode unit phasors. Expanded model: append ALL three pairwise products z[j]*conj(z[i]) for i<j, before time averaging. Real columns then imaginary columns. No phase sums, higher harmonics, delays, frequency/degree/window/seed search or hardcoded 27ms period.
observation: Original +/-10Hz zero-phase low observers, four forward Butterworth4 bands1200..2200/2200..4000/4000..8000/8000..14000Hz, trim12000frames each end, nonoverlap48frame means at48kHz. Reproduce parent native features/powers exactly. Difference features average the sample-level complex products, not products of averaged features.
fit: OLS on TRAIN only, each band divided by its own TRAIN mean, intercept and all12 expanded features. Retain complete coefficients, rank, condition, singular values. No ridge, clipping, coefficient attenuation or refit using check. Report conservative global lower/upper bound c +/- sum(hypot(a,b)); phase dependence makes lower>0 sufficient, not necessary. Do not turn a failed bound into proof of negative actual power.
prediction: Freeze each native/expanded model before check. Report constant/native/expanded MSE, correlation, mean, minimum prediction and residual power variance for both portions. Every same-PSD control gets the identical separate TRAIN-only nested fits; real check improvement must be positive and exceed every control's corresponding incremental improvement in at least3of4bands, plus full rank and positive expanded bound, for a future synthesis prerequisite. For each model/portion/control, T=P+R implies exact TT=PP+PR+RP+RR at every lag; also meanT=meanP+meanR. Preserve all terms and prediction errors.
